main_issue: How to handle D's strong-smelling sambal belacan cooking: ban it, use a window fan, or restrict cooking times (weekends or after 7pm).

A-B.evidence: A opposed strong-smelling cooking (T1) and doubted the fan (T11); B pushed the fan (T6, T12, T20). B accepted the time limit as only partial help (T18). Both want less smell but back different fixes.

A-C.evidence: C backs the fan (T9, T13, T21), A says a fan is not enough (T11). C says laundry is still affected after the time deal (T19). They never address each other directly.

A-D.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1) and D resisted (T4, T14). A proposed weekends or after 7pm (T15) and D agreed (T16); A thanked D (T17).

B-C.evidence: B changed the fan direction after C's laundry concern (T8), C accepted (T9). Both pushed the fan again together (T20, T21).

B-D.evidence: D doubted the fan and objected to setting one up each time (T10, T14). B kept pushing it (T12, T20). D never accepted the fan, and B did not accept the time compromise as sufficient (T18).

C-D.evidence: C backs the fan (T13, T21) while D doubts it (T10, T14). D accepted the time limit (T16), but C says the laundry problem remains (T19).
